title: Streaming JSON Contract Oracle and Decoder Fallback Matrix
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: As we expand JSON mode and constrained decoding across streaming+toolcall paths, we need a reproducible validation harness that behaves like a 'contract oracle' for partial streams. Current suites focus on final-output validators and full-stream regressions; they miss edge cases where a tool call is emitted mid-stream, or where the decoder's constrained policy triggers a fallback mid-response.

Objective: Build a test oracle and experiment matrix that systematically injects partial chunks, simulated transport reordering, intentional schema drift, and tool call boundaries to validate: 1) constrained decoder adherence to schema while streaming; 2) graceful fallback behaviors (e.g., emit sentinel + structured error + compact recovery path) when constraints are violated; 3) compatibility between streaming reassembly + tool-call metadata and our post-hoc JSON validator.

Scope: The ticket covers engineering the harness, a canonical set of test vectors, and a small benchmark to measure false-positive/negative rates for the oracle versus existing validators. It will not cover full CI integration for all model families (follow-up ticket).

Acceptance criteria: 1) A runnable harness (CLI + small API) that can: feed pre-chunked token sequences into the constrained decoder, simulate network chunk boundaries and mid-stream toolcall insertions, and produce a deterministic verdict per run. 2) A curated matrix of >=40 test vectors covering: valid partial streams, incomplete JSON chunks, toolcall-interleaved streams, intentional token corruption, and schema drift scenarios. 3) Clear pass/fail criteria and a baseline table of heuristic metrics (precision/recall) comparing the oracle to the existing JSON-mode post-hoc validator. 4) Documentation: README with how to run locally and how to add vectors.

Implementation notes: The harness will wrap the constrained decoder and streaming reassembler we already have; it will expose knobs for: chunk_size distribution, reorder_probability, toolcall_injection_points, and schema_strictness_level. The verdicts are three-state: PASSED, RECOVERED_WITH_WARNINGS, FAILED_STRICT. We expect to capture micro-failures where streaming reassembly misses the toolcall boundary and the constrained decoder does an unsafe fallback.

Test vectors: We'll create vectors from: curated real-world prompts (support ticket summarization, multi-toolchains), fuzzed sequences based on our model tokenization, and manual edge cases (e.g., nested objects where a closing brace is split across chunks). Each vector will include: original sequence, chunking profile, expected verdict, and tags.

Metrics and reporting: For each run we will emit counts of: total_tests, passed, recovered, failed_strict, average_time_per_run_ms, and top-5 failure reasons (e.g., truncated-key, midtoolcall-split, invalid-escape). We will persist results as CSV for quick visualization and attach a small HTML summary template to the harness.
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket created after discussion with PM and QA. Identified gap in streaming validation when tool calls are present mid-response.

2025-02-14 Marco Li: Spike complete — prototype can feed pre-chunked token streams into the constrained decoder. Found two classes of failure: (1) reassembly losing toolcall metadata, (2) decoder fallback emitting non-sentinel text that breaks downstream parsers.
2025-02-16 QA (Jordan Patel): Provided an initial list of 18 edge vectors derived from customer bug reports and incident traces. Suggested adding reordering and simulated retransmit tests.
2025-02-18 Design review (Riley Chen): Agreed on three-state verdicts and UI summary fields for Console. Suggested adding an option to emit a compact recovery patch that downstream apps can apply.

2025-02-20 Marco Li: Implemented CSV output and basic HTML summary. Running full matrix locally; current baseline shows 92% precision vs post-hoc validator on the seeded vectors. Next: expand fuzz corpus and harden reassembly logic.
